entities.text: High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The accused persons in C.C.No.9 of 2001 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class-II, Kottayam were convicted by the trial court under Sections 2(1a) (a) (m), 7(1) and 16(1)(a)
(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act r/w appendix B of Rule 5 item A.11.02.04 and A.11.01.11 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and sentenced them thereunder.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class-II, Kottayam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In the appeal, the conviction and sentence were set aside and the matter was remitted to the court below for proceeding with the case afresh, after framing charge in the light of the report received by the Central Food Laboratory.

2. Heard.
3. The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 18.11.1996 at about 10.45 a.m., PW1, the Food Inspector purchased 750 ml. of cow curd from the first accused.
The second accused was the licencee of the said restaurant.
After taking the sample as per law, one of the samples was sent to the Public Analyst.
The public analyst submitted Ext.P11 report stating that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow curd.
Thereafter, the complaint was filed before the trial court.
The trial court framed a charge and proceeded with the case.
While so, Ext.P13 report from the Central Food Laboratory was received.
The trial court considered the report of the Central Food Laboratory and convicted the revision petitioners.

However, the appellate court found that the trial court framed the charge not on the basis of the report of the Central Food Laboratory, but on the basis of the public analyst report, which was superseded by the report of the Central Food Laboratory by virtue of Section 13 (3) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and consequently, the appellate court set aside the conviction and sentence and remanded the case to the trial court.
Ext.P13 report would also show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for cow curd.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW3 were examined and Exts.P1 to P18 were marked for the prosecution.
No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioners.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioners has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P13 report cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.

The learned counsel for M.V.Cherian vs C.V.Abdul Jaleel on 11 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40616643/
2

the revision petitioners relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v.
Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text:
Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v.
Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P13 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case as adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).
A Division Bench of this Court in judgment dated 17-11-2015 in Crl.M.C. No. 417 of 2011 held that the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) is applicable to all cases.
In the said circumstances, the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below cannot be sustained.

7. In the said circumstances, even if a fresh trial is conducted after framing charge in the light of Ext.P13 report of the Central Food Laboratory, the trial is to be culminated in the acquittal of the accused in view of the violation of the mandatory provisions of Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.
In the said circumstances, the judgment of the appellate court remanding the case to the trial court cannot be sustained and consequently, I set aside the same.
However, the judgment of the appellate court setting aside the judgment of the trial court does not warrant any interference by this court.
In the result, this revision petition stands allowed as above and the revision petitioners are acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioners stand cancelled and they are set at liberty.
B. SUDHEENDRA KUMAR JUDGE Scl/11.01.2016
